description: Preparation of a custom concentration dextrose solution by mixing two different stock concentrations using the alligation method
clinicalUse: Customized parenteral nutrition or fluid therapy requiring specific dextrose concentration

prescriptionDetails.examplePrescription: Dextrose 7.5% solution, Make 1000 mL for parenteral nutrition base

formulation.beyondUseDate: 24 hours from preparation when stored at 2-8°C (per USP <797> for low-risk compounding)

dosageCalculations.calculation: Higher concentration (10%) and Lower concentration (5%) to achieve Desired concentration (7.5%)

dosageCalculations.step: Calculate parts of higher strength needed
Calculate parts of lower strength needed

equipment.name: Empty sterile IV bag or bottle

environment.notes: Sterile compounding in ISO 5 environment within ISO 7 buffer room

steps.description: Perform hand hygiene and don appropriate PPE (gown, gloves, hair cover, mask)
Clean laminar flow hood with 70% isopropyl alcohol
steps.notes: Allow to dry completely; hood should be running for at least 30 minutes before use

steps.description: Gather all materials and place in hood for staging
steps.notes: Remove outer packaging outside hood; bring only immediate containers into hood

steps.description: Disinfect all items entering the hood with 70% isopropyl alcohol
Allow all disinfected items to dry completely
steps.notes: Do not fan or blow on items

steps.description: Using aseptic technique, withdraw 500 mL of Dextrose 10% injection
steps.notes: Use multiple syringes if needed (e.g., 8-10 syringes of 50-60 mL each)

steps.description: Transfer the 500 mL of Dextrose 10% to the empty sterile container
Using aseptic technique, withdraw 500 mL of Dextrose 5% injection
Add the 500 mL of Dextrose 5% to the same container
steps.notes: Total volume should now be 1000 mL
Invert bag/bottle 10-15 times to ensure uniform mixing

steps.description: Inspect final product for particulate matter and clarity
steps.notes: Solution should be clear and colorless; no visible particles
Include all required labeling per institutional policy and USP <797>

visualInspection.notes: Inspected against black and white backgrounds under good lighting

sterilityConcerns.notes: Prepared under ISO 5 conditions using aseptic technique

osmolarity.notes: Hypertonic solution; verify appropriate for intended use

labeling.contents: Dextrose 7.5% in Water for Injection, 1000 mL
warnings: Check for particulate matter before use
labeling.additionalInfo: Lot numbers of component solutions documented in compounding record

safety.specialHandling: Sterile product - maintain aseptic technique at all times

dispensing.counselingNotes: Discussed with nursing: IV administration, storage requirements, expiration

counselingPoints: Store refrigerated until ready to use
Allow to warm to room temperature before administration if refrigerated
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before each use
Discard if particulates observed or container integrity compromised
Single-use container - discard any unused portion

stability.notes: Dextrose solutions are generally stable but prepared as sterile product must follow USP <797> beyond-use dating

references: Dering-Anderson AM. Pharmaceutical Calculations: A Conceptual Approach. Chapter 10: Alligation
Marriott JF. Pharmaceutical Compounding and Dispensing. 2nd ed. Chapter 11: Sterile Preparations
ASHP Guidelines on Compounding Sterile Preparations

notes.alligationApplication: Alligation is particularly useful when you need to prepare a concentration that falls between two available stock concentrations. This method ensures accurate calculation of the quantities needed from each stock solution.
notes.alternativeMethod: Could also calculate using dilution equation (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂ = C₃V₃), but alligation provides a systematic approach that's less prone to error.
notes.whyThisConcentration: 7.5% dextrose is commonly used in parenteral nutrition formulations as it provides appropriate calories while managing osmolarity.
notes.clinicalContext: This preparation demonstrates both alligation calculations and sterile compounding technique, combining two important compounding skills.

clinicalPearls: Always verify calculations using alternative method before compounding
1000 mL of 7.5% dextrose provides 75 g × 3.4 kcal/g = 255 kcal
Hypertonic dextrose solutions should be administered via central line when concentration >10%
Document lot numbers of all component solutions for traceability

conceptualApproach.rationale: When mixing two different concentrations to achieve a desired intermediate concentration, the alligation method provides a systematic way to calculate the proportions needed. The method is based on the principle that the amount of active ingredient must be conserved.
conceptualApproach.clinicalContext: Essential skill for preparing custom concentrations in hospital pharmacy, particularly for parenteral nutrition, pediatric formulations, and critical care applications where standard concentrations may not meet patient needs.
